title: The right conversation
lines: Imagine an agent that finds people who want to work on the same problem as you.
The Network of Intent proposes a network where personal agents compare needs before asking people to meet.
These agents would explain what you want now, what you can offer, and what must stay private.

emotionalPlan.purpose: A thousand introductions are useless when neither side knows what the other actually wants. The Network of Intent proposes personal agents that help the right conversations happen. Instead of polishing public profiles, they would represent current goals, constraints, and private preferences.

title: Private intentions
lines: A researcher needs a collaborator; a potential partner has expertise but little available time.
Finding that mismatch early could save both people another pointless meeting.
The book explores the trust, privacy, and business questions behind this possible network.

title: A network worth testing
lines: The proposal still needs to prove that people would find those introductions useful.
Could finding the right person begin with a conversation that actually understands what you need?

emotionalPlan.purpose: Its promise must survive real tests before the network deserves anyone’s attention. Could better representation make finding people feel less like searching and more like being understood?
